# Cite this material {.unnumbered .no-slide}

The book and the **{easyDR}** package live in the same repository and share a
version, so one citation covers both. If you used the package to fit something,
or the book to decide how, please cite it.

```{r}
#| echo: false
# strwrap keeps the line inside the content column, which a single cat() of
# the whole citation would run past.
citation_line <- paste0(
  "Antunes V (", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"), "). ",
  "Dose-Response Meta-Analysis: A hands-on guide, and the easyDR ",
  "package for R. Version ",
  as.character(utils::packageVersion("easyDR")), ". ",
  "https://github.com/vanioljantunes/easyDR"
)
writeLines(strwrap(citation_line, width = 64, exdent = 2))
```

For a reference manager, in BibTeX:

```bibtex
@manual{easydr,
  title  = {Dose-Response Meta-Analysis: A hands-on guide, and the
            {easyDR} package for {R}},
  author = {Vanio Antunes},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://github.com/vanioljantunes/easyDR},
  note   = {Book: https://vanioljantunes.github.io/easyDR/}
}
```

## What to cite alongside it {.unnumbered .no-slide}

**{easyDR}** prepares the data and reports the result. The estimation is done
by **{dosresmeta}** [@crippa2016], which in turn implements the method of
@greenland1992. A methods section that names only this package is incomplete,
so cite those two as well whenever you report a fitted curve.

Both packages carry their own citation, which _R_ will print on request:

```{r}
#| eval: false
citation("easyDR")
citation("dosresmeta")
```
